entries.def:
τύπτω 
[in LXX chiefly for hi. ;] 
to strike, smite, beat: with accusative, Mat.24.49, Mrk.15.19, Luk.12.45, Act.18.17; 21.32; 23.2-3; of mourners, τὰ στήθη, Luk.18.13; 23.48; ἐπὶ τ. σιαγόνα, Luk.6.29 εἰς τ. κεφαλήν, Mat.27.30. Metaphorical, of God inflicting evil: Act.23.3 (cf. Exo.8.2, Ezk.7.9, al.); of disquieting conscience, 1Co.8.12.†
(AS)

1. an absolute sovereign , unlimited by law or constitution, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: not applied to old hereditary sovereignties βασιλεῖαι); such as those of (Homer) or of Sparta; for the term rather regards the irregular way in which the power was gained , than the way in which it was exercised , being applied to the mild Pisistratus, but not to the despotic kings of Persia. However, the word soon came to…

τυρβάζω 
to disturb, trouble: pass., Luk.10.41, Rec. (WH, R, θορυβάζω).†
(AS)

Τύρος, -ου, ἡ 
Tyre, a maritime city of Phænicia: Mrk.7.31, Act.21.3, 7; Τ. κ, Σιδών, Mat.11.21-22; 15.21, Mrk.3.8; 7.24, Luk.6.17; 10.13-14.†
(AS)

τυφλός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX for עִוֵּר ;] 
blind: as subst., ὁ τ., Mat.9.27, Mrk.8.22, Luk.4.18" (LXX), Jhn.5.3, al. Metaphorical: Mat.15.14; 23.16-26, Jhn.9.39-41, Rom.2.19, 2Pe.1.9, Rev.3.17. 
(AS)

τυφλόω, -ῶ
(τυφλός), [in LXX: Isa.42.19 (עִוֵּר), Tob.7.7 א, Wis.2.21 א * ;] 
to blind, make blind: metaphorically, Jhn.12.40 (LXX, καμμύω), 2Co.4.4, 1Jn.2.11.†
(AS)

τυφόω, -ῶ
(τῦφος, smoke; metaphorically, conceit), 
prop., to wrap in smoke; used only metaphorically, to puff up, becloud with pride: pass., 1Ti.3.6; 6.4, 2Ti.3.4 (Dem., Arist., al.).†
(AS)

τύφω
(τῦφος, smoke), 
to raise a smoke; pass., to smoke: Mat.12.20 (LXX, καπνιζόμενον).†
(AS)

τυφωνικός, -ή, -όν
(τῦφων, a hurricane, typhoon) 
tempestuous: Act.27.14.†
(AS)
